The propaganda was elegant: Freedom through deregulation. Your bedroom is neutral territory. Your screen is sovereign soil. Sexual discipline is the enemy’s constraint. Restraint is psychological occupation. Liberation is the righteous campaign.

What the recruitment posters didn’t show: You weren’t being freed. You were being disarmed.

History has already run this experiment. J. D. Unwin recorded the results.

Unwin spent seven years analyzing eighty civilizations across five thousand years of human history. He started the research expecting to prove that sexual liberation catalyzed cultural flourishing. He was a rationalist, a social anthropologist operating in the optimistic glow of the Enlightenment project. He wanted the data to confirm what modernity promised: that throwing off sexual restraint would unleash human potential.

The data forced him to the opposite conclusion. He published it in 1934 as Sex and Culture, a dense, meticulous tome that tracked societies from tribal cultures to the Roman Empire, from Babylonian city-states to Anglo-Saxon England. The pattern emerged with mathematical consistency.

The conclusion: No society in human history has ever maintained its cultural energy beyond three generations after abandoning what he called “absolute monogamy,” the insistence on prenuptial and postnuptial continence. Not one. Eighty civilizations analyzed. Zero exceptions.

When a society maximizes sexual opportunity, it stops building. The cathedrals stop rising. The philosophy shallows. The territorial expansion halts. The art becomes self-referential instead of transcendent. Within three generations, the civilization enters what Unwin called “unrelieved monotony,” a low-energy state where survival replaces creation, maintenance replaces innovation, and the future becomes unimaginable.

Three generations. That’s the countdown.

Let’s start the clock.

Expansive Energy vs. Extraction Economics

Unwin identified a force he called “expansive energy,” the collective capacity to build, explore, invent, project will across time and space. This is the biological substrate that produces children, constructs cities, launches ships, writes symphonies, establishes universities that operate for centuries. It’s generative force operating at civilizational scale, the accumulated surplus of disciplined sexuality redirected toward legacy.

He contrasted this with societies that pursued what he termed “sexual opportunity,” the cultural permission to gratify sexual impulse without covenant constraint. These cultures didn’t disappear overnight. They didn’t burn in apocalyptic flames. They settled into what he described as “less strenuous” conditions. They maintained the forms, government, trade, religion, art, but the function inverted. The civilization stopped producing. It started consuming what previous generations had built.

Sound familiar?

Unwin’s data showed the pattern with precision: sexual energy is the same force that builds civilizations and produces children. When that force gets redirected toward immediate, frictionless gratification, it’s extracted from the future. You can’t spend generative capacity on dopamine hits and cathedral construction simultaneously. The body doesn’t work that way. The civilization doesn’t work that way.

His words, written in 1934:

“In human records, there is no instance of a society retaining its energy after a complete new generation has inherited a tradition which does not insist on pre-nuptial and post-nuptial continence.”

One generation to inherit the new pattern. Three generations and the collapse becomes structural, embedded so deeply in the culture that reversal requires civilizational death and rebirth.

Nobody reads Unwin now. The conclusion is too expensive.

The Western Countdown

The Sexual Revolution wasn’t spontaneous cultural evolution. It was constructed, funded, propagandized, legislated, and normalized across multiple domains simultaneously. The inflection point, the moment absolute monogamy was abandoned as cultural ideal, can be identified.

1965–1970: This is when the countdown began.

The Pill became widely available (1960, mass adoption by 1965). Roe v. Wade was still coming, but the legal groundwork was being laid. No-fault divorce began its state-by-state rollout (California first in 1969, spreading through the 1970s). Pornography was decriminalized through “artistic merit” legal challenges. Universities became laboratories for sexual experimentation, framed as political resistance and personal liberation.

The cultural messaging shifted: Free love as enlightenment. Monogamy reframed as possessive patriarchy. Sexual experimentation as self-discovery. Virginity as embarrassment. Restraint as repression requiring therapy.

The economic order shifted simultaneously: Women entering the workforce en masse, which destroyed the single-income household, which required two-income dependence, which eliminated the economic foundation for early family formation, which delayed marriage into the late twenties, which extended the window of sexual opportunity by a decade, which normalized serial short-term partnerships as the default relational pattern.

This was not accident. The people funding this transformation, Playboy Foundation, Kinsey Institute, Rockefeller Population Council, understood they were engineering a behavioral shift. They had access to the anthropology. They knew the historical pattern. But they chose profit over posterity.

Pornography as industry required the destruction of monogamy as market competition. Contraception as product required the destruction of fertility as default. The two-income trap required the destruction of the single-income household as economic viability.

They had read Unwin, or people who had. They understood the three-generation pattern. They built the infrastructure anyway.

The clock started ticking.

Generation 1 (1965-1990): This is the cohort born into and raised under the new sexual order. They are the first generation to inherit a tradition that does not insist on prenuptial continence.

Their parents, the ones who enacted the Sexual Revolution, still carried the guilt and conditioning of the old world. They remembered when sex had consequences, when community surveillance enforced boundaries, when marriage was expected by twenty-three. They rebelled against that world, but they were formed by it.

Generation 1 had no such formation. They were children of divorce. They were raised in households where sexual restraint was never articulated as virtue. They watched their parents cycle through partners, treating relationships as serial monogamy at best, overlapping chaos at worst. They received the cultural message through every available channel: Your body. Your choice. No judgment. Explore your sexuality. Don’t let anyone shame you.

This first generation still retained some of the civilizational energy. They could still build, though less ambitiously than their grandparents. They still formed families, though later, more fragile, more prone to dissolution. They still pursued long-term projects, though with less confidence in permanence.

Why? Because they still had living memory of the old world through their grandparents. They could observe the contrast. They saw what stability looked like, even if they couldn’t replicate it. The cultural energy hadn’t fully dissipated. The generative fire was sputtering, but still burning.

This generation came of age in the 1980s and 1990s. They built the internet. They constructed the last wave of infrastructure we’re still using.

Generation 2 (1990-2015): This is the generation that encountered weaponized internet pornography during their formative years.

Broadband arrived in the late 1990s. Tube sites launched in 2006-2007, making high-speed, high-definition pornography instantly available, infinitely varied, completely free. The biological hijacking began at scale.

This generation inherited no memory of the old world. Their grandparents, the pre-1965 cohort who still operated under absolute monogamy, were distant figures, relics of a world that seemed incomprehensible. Waiting until marriage? Unthinkable. Virginity as virtue? Absurd. Sexual restraint? Therapy material.

They were born into hookup culture as default. Dating apps optimized the sexual marketplace for frictionless transactions. Sex became the expected outcome of a third date, second date, first date, first message. Commitment became the aberration requiring justification.

This is the generation that cannot build.

They can’t buy houses, not just because of economics, but because they can’t imagine permanence. They’re not forming families, fertility rates collapsed to sub-replacement across the developed world. They’re not producing culture with longevity, everything is content, churned out for algorithmic consumption, forgotten in a week.

This is the generation Unwin called “unrelieved monotony.” They manage systems they didn’t build. They consume resources they didn’t generate. They critique the past without constructing a future. The cathedrals are crumbling, and they’re arguing about pronouns.

The expansive energy is gone.

Generation 3 (2015-present): We’re here now. This is the generation entering sexual maturity in a world where the average age of first pornography exposure is eleven years old.

The reward system gets captured before the soul develops language for resistance. Before conscience takes shape. Before the will is strengthened through any meaningful discipline. Before they’ve experienced a single relationship in physical reality, they’ve already consumed thousands of hours of supernormal sexual stimulus.

This generation has never known a world where infinite sexual novelty wasn’t available instantly. They have never experienced the sexual tension that builds toward covenant. They have never seen a civilization in its ascent, only its managed descent.

Unwin’s countdown completes here. Three generations after the Sexual Revolution, the civilization has lost the capacity to build anything that requires generational investment. They can’t imagine children. They can’t imagine marriage lasting. They can’t imagine a building project that takes thirty years. They can’t imagine a future different from the present, except worse.

When you uproot the generative principle, the civilization doesn’t continue with slightly different values. It stops building and enters survival mode.

We’re watching it happen in real time.

The Weapon System

Pornography isn’t a vice. It’s a counterfeit temple.

Stripping away every element that makes sex fruitful and replacing it with simulation that cannot produce life.

Risk is removed. Consequence is removed. Covenant is removed. Investment is removed. Delay is removed. Relationship is removed. What remains is the shadow of the act, a ghost that mimics the form while reversing the function.

The human appetite for sexual union exists because union produces children, families, futures. The desire points toward something real, the co-creation of life with another person in covenant before God. That desire is woven into the body as testimony to divine design.

But introduce infinite shadows. Unlimited counterfeits. Zero cost for consumption. The soul begins responding to phantoms. There’s no offspring. No relationship. No legacy. Just the hunger, repeated until the soul stops recognizing what it was actually hungry for.

The philosophical term is “desire misdirection.” The practical term is “the inability to build anything that requires hope in the future.”

The civilization loses the capacity to construct anything that outlasts a season. Marriage becomes unthinkable. Children become burden rather than blessing. Cathedral construction becomes incomprehensible. The future becomes unimaginable because generative desire has been redirected toward sterile repetition.

The conditioning operates at the level of desire itself. The economic model is industrial. The delivery is frictionless. And the result, three generations after normalization, is exactly what Unwin predicted: unrelieved monotony. A civilization that can no longer imagine its own future because it has lost contact with its own seed.

The Medical Permission Structure

To ensure voluntary participation, they needed a permission story. You can’t openly market a spiritual weapon as a spiritual weapon. You need a therapeutic narrative.

Enter the prostate health mythology.

The narrative: Frequent ejaculation is biological necessity. Your body requires regular release to prevent disease, discomfort, dangerous accumulation. Retention causes harm. The studies say so. Doctors recommend it. It’s health maintenance, not spiritual discipline.

What the studies bury: The male body is a closed covenant system designed for conservation and reclamation. Spermatogenesis takes 64-74 days. Unreleased seed doesn’t accumulate like waste requiring disposal. It’s broken down and reabsorbed, proteins, minerals, life-giving elements, all of it returned to nourish the body that created it. The design assumes conservation, not constant depletion.

The medical studies also ignore the soul-level destruction inherent in chronic use:

  • Desire dysregulation: The same disorder of appetite seen in addiction, the inability to delay gratification, the loss of motivation for difficult good, the collapse of will.
  • Shame as chronic condition: The secrecy, the fear of discovery, the internal accusation, this keeps the soul in permanent state of stress, which destroys rest, destroys peace, destroys the capacity for joy.
  • The withdrawal from embodied life: Each session replaces physical presence with digital absence, actual relationship replaced by simulation, real labor replaced by passive consumption, embodied community replaced by isolated fantasy.
  • The severing of sleep from rest: Late-night use violates the body’s natural rhythm, which destroys the hormonal order that makes a man capable of strength, which destroys motivation, which creates the descending spiral.
  • The flattening of desire: When the soul receives counterfeit pleasure from pixels, it stops seeking real pleasure from achievement, covenant, creation. Reality becomes inadequate. The wife becomes dull compared to the infinite novelty of the screen.

They measure one variable, ejaculation frequency and cancer correlation, and ignore the comprehensive ruin.

This is how you convince a man that his body requires the very act that depletes his soul.

Same move as the serpent’s offer in the Garden: reframe the violation as wisdom, the boundary as oppression, the destructive path as liberation.

Hookup Culture as Physical Liturgy

The screen conditioning moved into physical reality through hookup culture, the embodied liturgy of the same spiritual rebellion.

This is immediacy worship: pleasure now, investment never, covenant as obstacle to overcome. Seed scattered across encounters that produce no children, no depth, no bonds that compound across time. Sex as consumption. Bodies as interchangeable commodities. Intimacy as friction to be eliminated.

The culture inverted every signal:

  • “Body count” became status symbol instead of testimony to relational devastation.
  • Virginity became embarrassment instead of preserved treasure.
  • Restraint became pathology instead of strength.

And the ones performing best in this economy, the ones accumulating the highest numbers, were celebrated as victors.

Unwin saw this pattern in every civilization he studied:

“The limitation of the sexual opportunity has been an important condition of cultural advance.”

He wasn’t preaching. He was documenting.

Societies that maintained boundaries around sexual expression poured that force into creation. Societies that removed those boundaries entered entropy.

By maximizing sexual opportunity, we didn’t liberate desire. We severed it from its telos, its proper end and purpose.

The Sexual Revolution promised liberation but delivered bondage. Women were told they could approach sex like men, without attachment, without consequence, without cost. But feminine nature doesn’t work that way. The body releases oxytocin during intimacy, creating bonds whether the mind consents or not.

Each casual encounter leaves scar tissue. Each betrayal makes the next covenant harder to trust. The heart learns to protect itself by refusing to open.

Men were told they could have infinite variety without responsibility. But masculine nature doesn’t work that way either. Desire becomes habituated to novelty. The real woman, with her ordinary face, her aging body, her demands for faithfulness, cannot compete with the infinite variety of fantasy.

The soul learns to prefer the controllable image over the uncontrollable person.

Both sexes were sold an economy that functions for perhaps five years, from eighteen to twenty-three, when youth and novelty make the lies feel sustainable. Then reality arrives. Women encounter the biological clock. Men encounter the void where purpose should be. And both discover they’ve been spending seed capital they needed to plant a future.

The men at the top understood this:

  • The Rockefellers funding population control.
  • The Playboy Foundation normalizing promiscuity as sophistication.
  • The pharmaceutical companies marketing contraception as freedom.
  • The technology platforms monetizing desire itself.

They had access to the anthropology. They had read Unwin, or funded those who had.

But they chose profit over posterity. Present wealth over future generations. Shareholder dividends over their own grandchildren’s inheritance.

This was the ancient trade: Esau’s bargain, selling the birthright for immediate satisfaction.
